The test image shows a young seedling that has collapsed/wilted at the soil line with what appears to be stem rot. Other healthy seedlings are visible nearby on sandy soil. Key features: seedling collapse, damping-off pattern.

Top candidates: Pythium_damping_off, Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora. Let me check reference images.

Analyzing key features from the test image:
- Young seedling collapsed/wilted at soil line on sandy soil
- Stem shows tan/yellowish damage at the collapse point (shepherd's crook shape)
- Other healthy seedlings visible nearby
- Dry appearance (not soft/water-soaked)

**Comparison:**
- **Pythium_damping_off**: Shows very soft, water-soaked brown rot at cotyledon stage — the test seedling looks drier/firmer
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows reddish-brown, sunken, firm and dry lesions at soil line; the reference bottom-right panel shows very similar seedling collapse on sandy soil — best match
- **Phytophthora**: Shows dark brown lesion extending upward from taproot, usually more established plants

The dry-looking collapse at the soil line on sandy soil, without the wet/soft appearance of Pythium, aligns with Rhizoctonia. The Rhizoctonia reference image shows nearly identical seedling collapse in sandy soil conditions.
